Aliases: Cinema dark|Dark media app|OLED dark UI|Streaming dark
Keywords: dark, cinema, media, oled, streaming, poster, immersive, mobile
Looks Like: Near-black screens where posters, stills and video carry the colour. Controls sit low on the screen and stay out of the picture's way.
Use When: film app, streaming, video, photography, music player, ticketing, event listings, gallery
Avoid When: Text-heavy tools and forms used in daylight, where a dark screen is hard to read. Also poor for users who find light text on black tiring.
Palette: Charcoal base so the artwork supplies the colour, with one warm accent for the play or buy action. Base #0E0F12, surface #181A1F, text #ECE9E4, accent #E8A33D, muted #9A9AA3.
Type Approach: Pair a condensed or sharp display face such as Bebas Neue or Oswald for titles with DM Sans for body. Body 16px at 1.5 line height; titles large and few.
Layout: Full-bleed artwork, a single column, a bottom tab bar of 4-5 items inside the safe area, and 48px targets. Titles overlay images only on a darkened strip.
Motion: Poster-to-detail shared transition at 280ms ease-out; press feedback at 100ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Pure #000 text boxes on pure white text; grey-on-black captions too faint to read; a glow behind every poster; a purple gradient hero
Accessibility: Light text on near-black can halate for some readers, so keep body at least 16px and weight 400 or above. Check 4.5:1 for body text (1.4.3) and 3:1 for controls and focus rings (1.4.11). Never place text straight on photos without a scrim. Keep video autoplay off or muted with a pause control (2.2.2).
Performance: medium: large images and video; serve sized, compressed posters and lazy-load below the fold.
Checklist: Text on artwork has a scrim; tab bar clears the home indicator; muted text passes 4.5:1; autoplay is off or has a pause control; targets are 48px

Aliases: SaaS app mobile|Product app UI|Boutique tech
Keywords: saas, app, product, mobile, boutique, onboarding, clean, tech
Looks Like: A small, precise product app: one strong colour, generous spacing, sharp type and a few well-chosen screens. It feels made for one job.
Use When: startup app, subscription product, productivity app, booking tool, small team tool, mobile onboarding
Avoid When: Dense data work that needs many columns, or brands that want warmth and play. A tidy look with no point of view reads as generic.
Palette: One confident brand colour on a cool light base, with a dark ink for text. Base #F6F7F9, ink #14171C, brand #2F5BEA, success #1E8E5A, line #D9DDE3.
Type Approach: Use Manrope or Plus Jakarta Sans for headings and Source Sans 3 for body, so headings and body differ in weight and shape. Body 16px, headings 600.
Layout: One column with a 16px side margin, a bottom tab bar, and a primary action pinned in the thumb zone. Sections vary in height; avoid a stack of equal cards.
Motion: Sheet slides up in 240ms ease-out; button press scales to 0.98 in 90ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Three icon cards in a row; a purple-to-blue gradient hero; a mock phone screen too small to read; the same rounded card repeated down the page
Accessibility: Brand blue on light must reach 4.5:1 as text (1.4.3). Keep 44px minimum targets (2.5.8), visible focus on keyboard and switch use (2.4.7), and text that reflows when zoomed to 200% (1.4.4).
Performance: low: mostly text and vector UI; keep to one font family pair and a few weights.
CSS Starter:
.btn { min-height: 48px; padding: 0 20px; background: var(--brand); color: #fff; border-radius: var(--radius); }
.btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--ink); outline-offset: 2px; }
Checklist: One primary action per screen in thumb reach; no identical card grid; real product screenshots; focus rings visible; contrast passes on brand colour

Aliases: Console UI|Command line app|Hacker mobile|Dev tool mobile
Keywords: terminal, cli, console, monospace, developer, logs, command, mobile
Looks Like: A phone screen styled as a console: monospace text, a prompt line, plain borders and no rounding. Output scrolls in a column and commands are buttons.
Use When: developer tool, server monitor, git client, log viewer, api tester, hacker game, technical audience
Avoid When: General consumers, older users and any content that is mostly prose. Monospace body text is slow to read in long passages.
Palette: Dark base with one phosphor-style text colour and one warning colour. Base #0C0F0C, text #C8F0C8, dim #6E8F6E, warn #F2B84B, error #FF6B5E.
Type Approach: Use JetBrains Mono or IBM Plex Mono, only for code, logs and data; set prose in IBM Plex Sans. Mono at 14-15px with 1.5 line height.
Layout: Single column, full-width rows, 12px gutters, a command bar docked above the keyboard, bottom actions in the thumb zone. Square corners, 1px borders.
Motion: New log lines appear instantly or with a 120ms step; cursor blink at 1000ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change. Stop the cursor blink.
Slop Habits: Monospace for every word including marketing copy; a pulsing green live dot with nothing live; fake code labels like ~/about as decoration; ASCII-art images
Accessibility: Green on black passes easily but dim text often fails; check 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Long unbroken lines must wrap or scroll without hiding content (1.4.10). Give each command button a 44px target (2.5.8) and a name for screen readers; do not rely on colour alone for errors.
Performance: low: text-only screens and system fonts load fast; limit log length with windowed lists.
CSS Starter:
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--fg); font: 15px/1.5 var(--font); }
.row { border: var(--border); border-radius: 0; padding: 12px; min-height: 44px; }
Checklist: Mono used only for code and data; prose is readable; dim text passes 4.5:1; errors are not colour-only; cursor blink stops on reduced motion

Aliases: Moving brutalism|Motion brutalist|Raw motion UI
Keywords: brutalism, kinetic, motion, raw, bold, marquee, oversized, mobile
Looks Like: Huge type, hard edges, flat blocks of colour and type that slides, stretches or scrolls. It is loud on purpose, with controls that stay plain.
Use When: music festival, fashion drop, art project, student portfolio, creative studio, launch event
Avoid When: Banking, health, government or anything calm and trusted. Constant movement also fails users with vestibular conditions unless it can be stopped.
Palette: Hard flat colour with black ink and one shouting accent. Paper #F2F0E8, ink #0A0A0A, signal #FF3B1D, block #2540FF, highlight #F7E600.
Type Approach: Use Archivo Black or Anton for display at 18vw or more on key lines, and Work Sans for body. Keep body static and 16px; only display lines move.
Layout: Edge-to-edge blocks, uneven column widths, text that bleeds off the right edge on one section only. Actions are full-width bars at the bottom.
Motion: One marquee line at 20s linear and one scroll-linked stretch; taps respond in 80ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change. Show the marquee text static.
Slop Habits: Every heading in all caps; marquee text on every section; sections that slide in on scroll the same way each time; heavy black borders around every block
Accessibility: Moving text can breach 2.2.2 and 2.3.3; give a visible pause control and honour reduced motion. Keep body copy still. Contrast of accent on paper must reach 4.5:1 for text (1.4.3). Oversized words must still reflow at 400% zoom (1.4.10).
Performance: medium: scroll-linked motion costs frames; animate transform only and keep one moving element per screen.
Checklist: Marquee has a pause control; reduced motion stops all movement; body text is static; contrast on signal colour passes; words reflow at 400%

Aliases: Flat UI mobile|Flat touch|Solid colour UI
Keywords: flat, touch, solid, simple, icons, colour, no-shadow, mobile
Looks Like: Solid colour fields, simple shapes and clear icons, with no shadows or textures. Hierarchy comes from size and colour alone.
Use When: utility app, kids app, quick tool, transit app, weather, first app, small team with no designer
Avoid When: Products where the screen needs depth cues, such as many layered panels. Flat surfaces can hide which things are tappable.
Palette: A few saturated, distinct colours on flat white or tinted fields. White #FFFFFF, teal #0E9F8E, coral #F2635A, sun #F5B82E, ink #1D2733.
Type Approach: Use Nunito or Poppins for headings with Nunito Sans for body. Weight 700 for headings and 400 for body; 16px minimum.
Layout: Large tappable blocks in a 2-column grid on phones, 16px gaps, bottom tab bar, and 48px or taller controls. Icons paired with text labels.
Motion: Colour fill change in 120ms; page change slides 220ms ease-out. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Pastel boxes in a grid of identical rounded cards; emoji as icons; icon tile above every heading; white text on a yellow fill
Accessibility: Without shadows or borders, tappable things must still look tappable: use a filled shape or underline (1.4.11 for the shape edge at 3:1). White text on teal or coral often fails 4.5:1, so test each pair (1.4.3). Use 44px minimum targets (2.5.8).
Performance: low: flat shapes and vector icons are small to download.
CSS Starter:
.tile { background: var(--teal); color: #fff; border-radius: var(--radius); min-height: var(--tap); box-shadow: none; }
.tile:active { background: #0B7F72; }
Checklist: Every tappable item looks tappable without shadow; text on each colour passes 4.5:1; icons have labels; targets are 48px; tiles differ in size

Aliases: Material You Expressive|M3 Expressive|Google Material mobile
Keywords: material, google, android, m3, expressive, components, dynamic colour, mobile
Looks Like: Google's Material 3 design system, with its expressive update: stronger shape, colour and motion, and components that follow the platform. Think of it as the native Android look.
Use When: android app, google ecosystem, flutter app, compose app, material web app, teams already on material
Avoid When: Brands with a strong own identity that Material's shapes would flatten, or iOS-first products where it feels foreign. Do not imitate it by hand.
Palette: Colour comes from a tonal scheme built from one seed colour, with surface, primary and container roles. Use the official generator, then check values such as primary #6750A4, surface #FEF7FF, on-surface #1D1B20.
Type Approach: Material uses Roboto, or Roboto Flex, with its own type roles (display, headline, title, body, label). Take sizes from the official type scale rather than choosing your own.
Layout: Follow the system's window size classes, 8dp spacing steps, navigation bar at the bottom on compact screens, and 48dp touch targets.
Motion: Use the system's own motion tokens and spring-based transitions, which are shipped with the components. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Copying the look with hand-written CSS and the wrong tokens; a floating action button on every screen; purple scheme left on default; mixing in other design systems
Accessibility: The official components carry tested contrast, focus and target sizes; keep them and check any custom colour at 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Dynamic colour can lower contrast, so test it. Do not shrink targets below 48dp (2.5.8).
Performance: medium: the component libraries are large; import only the parts used and tree-shake.
CSS Starter:
/* Use the official Material Web or Compose components; this is only a fallback. */
.card { background: var(--surface); color: var(--on-surface); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); padding: 16px; }
Checklist: Official Material components and tokens used, not copied; colour scheme generated from a brand seed; dark scheme tested; targets 48dp; reduced motion tested

Aliases: Neubrutalism|Neo-brutalist UI|Hard shadow UI
Keywords: neobrutalism, hard shadow, thick border, flat, bold, playful, colour, mobile
Looks Like: Thick black outlines, flat bright fills and hard offset shadows with no blur. It feels like a sticker sheet that you can tap.
Use When: indie app, creator tool, student project, game, community app, youth brand, playful startup
Avoid When: Finance, health or legal products that need to feel calm and serious. Too many outlined boxes also bury the main action.
Palette: Flat bright fills on an off-white page, each framed in black. Page #FFF8E7, ink #111111, pink #FF7AB6, mint #5BE3A8, sky #6EC1FF.
Type Approach: Use Space Grotesk or Bricolage Grotesque for headings at weight 700, and Public Sans for body. Body 16px; headings 24-40px.
Layout: Single column with 16px margins, blocks 2px-3px bordered, 4px offset shadow, big bottom buttons. Mix block widths; do not box everything.
Motion: On press, the shadow collapses and the block shifts 4px in 90ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change. Use a colour change instead of a shift.
Slop Habits: A bordered box around every block; a grid of identical rounded cards; pill badges used as decoration; tilted stickers on every section
Accessibility: Black borders help edge contrast (1.4.11), but bright fills with black text still need 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Keep focus rings visible beyond the hard shadow (2.4.7). Targets of 48px (2.5.8).
Performance: low: borders and flat fills cost almost nothing to draw.
CSS Starter:
.btn { background: var(--pink); border: var(--border); box-shadow: var(--shadow); min-height: 48px; }
.btn:active { box-shadow: 0 0 0 #111111; transform: translate(4px, 4px); }
Checklist: Only key blocks are outlined; shadows are hard, not blurred; text on fills passes 4.5:1; focus ring visible; press state works without motion

Aliases: Type-led mobile|Poster type UI|Big type app
Keywords: typography, poster, large type, editorial, headline, contrast, type-led, mobile
Looks Like: Screens built from a few huge words, with little else. Size, weight and spacing make the layout, and images are used sparingly.
Use When: campaign page, event app, magazine, quote app, personal brand, launch teaser, cultural venue
Avoid When: Data-heavy tools, long forms and shops with many products. Huge type pushes content below the fold and can break on long words.
Palette: Two or three colours at strong contrast so the type is the image. Paper #FAF7F2, ink #101010, accent #D9381E, support #1F4D3A.
Type Approach: Use a distinctive display face such as Fraunces or Playfair Display for headlines (pick one for a reason from the brand) with Libre Franklin for body. Scale headlines with clamp().
Layout: One column, headline at 12-16vw, body at 17-18px, wide left margin, and one element that breaks the grid. Buttons are full-width at the bottom.
Motion: Words reveal line by line over 400ms ease-out on first load only. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Tight negative letter-spacing on every heading; a single italic word in every title; ALL CAPS subtitles; a full stop after every headline
Accessibility: Check that very large words fit at 320px and reflow at 400% (1.4.10). Heading text must stay real text, not images (1.4.5). Ensure 4.5:1 for body and the accent (1.4.3). Allow text-resize (1.4.4).
Performance: low: type-led pages use few images; subset the display font and load only needed weights.
CSS Starter:
.hero { font: 700 clamp(3rem, 14vw, 7rem)/0.95 'Fraunces', serif; color: var(--ink); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
.lede { font-size: 1.125rem; max-width: var(--measure); }
Checklist: Longest word fits at 320px; headline is text not image; one grid break only; accent text passes 4.5:1; body is still 17px or more

Aliases: Scholarly UI|University app|Library app|Dark academia light
Keywords: academia, scholarly, library, university, serif, reading, study, mobile
Looks Like: A reading-first layout with serif text, ruled lines, footnote-style details and a muted, bookish palette. It looks like a well-set page.
Use When: university app, library, journal, study app, museum guide, archive, reading app, course portal
Avoid When: Fast-moving consumer or entertainment products. A dense serif page can be heavy on small screens if set poorly.
Palette: Ink on warm-neutral paper with one deep accent such as oxblood or navy. Paper #F4F0E6, ink #231F1B, oxblood #7B1E2B, navy #1E3350, rule #CFC6B2.
Type Approach: Use Source Serif 4 or Newsreader for body and headings at 17-19px, with Source Sans 3 for controls and labels. Line height 1.6, measure 55-70 characters.
Layout: One column, generous margins, hanging notes, ruled section breaks used sparingly, a bottom bar for library, search and account.
Motion: Section opens with a 200ms fade; no other motion. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Cream background with a clay accent as a default; drop caps on every section; italics in most headings; faux-parchment texture behind text
Accessibility: Serif body at small sizes can be hard for some readers, so keep 17px or larger and allow zoom (1.4.4). Check ruled-line and muted note colours at 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Keep links underlined and 44px apart (2.5.8).
Performance: low: text and a couple of font files; subset the serif.
CSS Starter:
body { background: var(--paper); color: var(--ink); font: 1.0625rem/var(--leading) 'Source Serif 4', serif; }
.prose { max-width: var(--measure); margin-inline: auto; padding: 0 16px; }
Checklist: Body 17px or more; line length 55-70 characters; links underlined; no parchment texture behind text; the cream and clay habit avoided unless the brand asks

Aliases: Cyberpunk UI|Sci-fi HUD|Neon HUD|Game HUD mobile
Keywords: cyberpunk, hud, neon, sci-fi, game, overlay, scanline, mobile
Looks Like: A heads-up display look: angular panels, thin lines, data readouts and neon accents on a dark field. Clipped corners replace rounding.
Use When: game companion app, esports, sci-fi brand, music event, gaming community, hardware launch, AR overlay
Avoid When: Anything that needs trust or long reading. Neon on black tires the eye and can cause glare for many users.
Palette: Dark base with two electric colours used for state, never for body text. Base #080A12, panel #121626, cyan #19E3FF, magenta #FF2E88, text #E6EAF5.
Type Approach: Use Rajdhani or Orbitron for headings and readouts, and Exo 2 or Barlow for body. Readouts in mono only for numbers; body 16px.
Layout: Angular panels with clipped corners, a single column, readouts in a 2-column strip, bottom command bar in thumb reach, 48px targets.
Motion: Panels switch on with a 160ms opacity change; one scanline loop at 6s on the header only. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change. Remove the scanline.
Slop Habits: Near-black with one acid accent and a glow behind everything; purple-to-blue gradients; glitch text on every heading; ASCII art and halftone as decoration
Accessibility: Neon on black can fail on thin lines, so keep text 4.5:1 (1.4.3) and UI lines 3:1 (1.4.11). Flicker and glitch effects can trigger seizures; never flash more than three times a second (2.3.1) and honour reduced motion (2.3.3).
Performance: medium: filters and blur are costly on phones; use flat colours and clip-path instead of heavy glow.
CSS Starter: .panel { background: var(--panel); border: 1px solid var(--cyan); clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - var(--cut)) 0, 100% var(--cut), 100% 100%, 0 100%); }
Checklist: Neon is used for state only; no flashing; body text passes 4.5:1; glow limited or absent; clip-path panels still have visible focus

Aliases: Crypto wallet UI|DeFi app|Web3 mobile|Bitcoin wallet
Keywords: bitcoin, defi, crypto, wallet, finance, web3, trading, mobile
Looks Like: A wallet or exchange app on a dark field with orange for Bitcoin and clear numeric readouts. Balances, fees and addresses are big and exact.
Use When: crypto wallet, exchange, defi dashboard, bitcoin app, staking, payments, portfolio tracker
Avoid When: Plain consumer banking or first-time savers who need reassurance rather than trading energy. Do not show invented numbers or fake live prices.
Palette: Dark graphite with Bitcoin orange as the only warm colour and green and red for change. Base #101114, panel #1A1C21, orange #F7931A, gain #2FBF71, loss #F0584F.
Type Approach: Use IBM Plex Sans for UI and IBM Plex Mono for amounts and addresses only. Tabular figures for all numbers.
Layout: Single column, balance at the top, bottom tabs for wallet, send, receive and activity, with a primary Send or Receive pair in thumb reach.
Motion: Number change eases in 200ms; confirmation sheet slides up 240ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: A pulsing green live dot when nothing is live; purple-to-blue gradient cards; glowing coin imagery; invented stats and rates
Accessibility: Never use colour alone for gain and loss; add a sign or arrow (1.4.1). Addresses need to be copyable and readable by screen readers. Confirm sends with a clear step and 44px targets (2.5.8). Contrast 4.5:1 for amounts (1.4.3).
Performance: medium: live prices and charts need updates; throttle refreshes and avoid heavy chart libraries.
CSS Starter:
.amount { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 2rem; color: var(--text); }
.send { background: var(--btc); color: #101114; min-height: 48px; border-radius: 8px; }
Checklist: Gain and loss not colour-only; amounts use tabular figures; addresses copyable; every number is from the real source; send needs a confirm step

Aliases: Clay UI|3D clay|Soft inflated UI
Keywords: clay, soft, 3d, rounded, playful, inflated, pastel, mobile
Looks Like: Puffy, rounded shapes with soft inner light and a gentle drop shadow, as if moulded from clay. Colours are friendly and the corners are large.
Use When: kids app, learning app, habit tracker, wellness check-in, toy brand, friendly onboarding
Avoid When: Data-dense or serious products, and any layout with many controls close together. Soft shapes lose edge contrast quickly.
Palette: Mid-light pastels with a deeper tone of the same hue for shade. Base #F3EEFF, clay blue #7AA2FF, clay peach #FFB59A, deep #3B2F63, shade #C9BFE8.
Type Approach: Use Fredoka or Baloo 2 for headings, and Nunito for body. Weight 600 headings; body 16-17px with 1.5 line height.
Layout: Large rounded blocks, 20-28px radius, 16px gaps, one chunky primary button in the thumb zone, 48px or taller.
Motion: Press squashes the shape to 0.97 over 120ms with a soft rebound of 180ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: A squircle on every element; a grid of identical rounded cards; blurry glow blobs behind the hero; pastels at many tints
Accessibility: Soft shadows do not give 3:1 edge contrast, so add a clear fill or border for controls (1.4.11). Text on pastel fills needs 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Keep a visible focus ring (2.4.7).
Performance: medium: layered shadows on many elements are costly; limit to key controls.
CSS Starter: .clay { background: var(--clay-blue); border-radius: var(--radius); box-shadow: var(--lift), inset 0 4px 6px #ffffff66; min-height: 48px; }
Checklist: Controls have an edge visible at 3:1; text on pastel passes 4.5:1; shadows limited to key controls; not every element is puffy

Aliases: Business app mobile|B2B mobile|Corporate app
Keywords: enterprise, b2b, business, admin, approvals, dense, workflow, mobile
Looks Like: A sober, information-first app for staff: lists, status labels, filters and approvals, with tidy type and limited colour.
Use When: hr app, field service, approvals, internal tool, crm, expense app, operations, banking staff app
Avoid When: Consumer brands or campaign pages that need personality. A neutral look with no clear structure becomes forgettable and hard to scan.
Palette: Neutral greys with one action colour and clear status colours. Base #FFFFFF, grey #F3F4F6, ink #1F2937, action #1D4ED8, warning #B45309, danger #B91C1C.
Type Approach: Use IBM Plex Sans or Source Sans 3 across the app, with different weights for hierarchy. Table text 14-15px; body 16px; numbers tabular.
Layout: Lists with 56px rows, sticky header, filters in a bottom sheet, bottom bar for 3-4 main areas, safe areas respected, and swipe actions that also have a button.
Motion: Row expand 160ms ease-out; status change uses colour and text, no motion needed. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: A bordered box around every block; a divider between every list item; dashboards of identical stat cards; a tiny gradient on every button
Accessibility: Status needs text or icon as well as colour (1.4.1). Keep 44px targets in dense lists (2.5.8) and offer a non-swipe route to every action. Check focus order in sheets and dialogs (2.4.3) and zoom to 200% (1.4.4).
Performance: low: mostly text lists; paginate long lists and virtualise rows.
CSS Starter:
.row { min-height: var(--row); display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 16px; }
.status { font-weight: 600; color: var(--warning); }
Checklist: Status shown by text as well as colour; every swipe action has a button; rows are 44px or taller; filters work in a sheet; numbers are tabular

Aliases: Hand-drawn UI|Doodle UI|Pencil sketch app
Keywords: sketch, hand-drawn, doodle, pencil, wobbly, paper, friendly, mobile
Looks Like: Wobbly outlines, pencil-like strokes and hand lettering on a paper ground, as if the screen were a notebook page.
Use When: note app, kids learning, craft brand, whiteboard tool, brainstorming, indie game, children's book
Avoid When: Banking, medical and enterprise tools. Hand lettering is slow to read in long text and is hard to localise.
Palette: Pencil grey ink on warm paper with two marker colours. Paper #FBF8F1, pencil #2B2B2B, marker red #E0524A, marker blue #3A6FD8, highlight #FFE97A.
Type Approach: Use Patrick Hand or Caveat for short headings only and Atkinson Hyperlegible or Nunito for body. Never set paragraphs in a handwriting face.
Layout: Single column with slightly uneven spacing, borders drawn with SVG or border-radius tricks, large buttons at the bottom, 48px targets.
Motion: Outlines redraw in 300ms with stroke-dashoffset on first view only. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Handwriting font for all body text; tilted cards in a grid of identical rounded cards; doodle icons that are unclear; texture too busy behind text
Accessibility: Handwriting faces cut readability, so use them for headings under 6 words and keep body in a plain face (1.4.8 advice). Check pencil lines at 3:1 for controls (1.4.11) and text at 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Keep decorative SVG hidden from assistive tools.
Performance: low: SVG strokes are small; avoid large paper textures.
CSS Starter:
.sketch { border: 2px solid var(--pencil); border-radius: var(--wobble); background: var(--paper); min-height: 48px; }
h1 { font-family: 'Patrick Hand', cursive; }
Checklist: Handwriting only on short headings; body is a plain face; line edges reach 3:1; texture is plain behind text; decorative SVG hidden from screen readers

Aliases: Soft UI|Neomorphic|Soft extruded UI
Keywords: neumorphism, soft ui, extruded, shadow, monochrome, tactile, minimal, mobile
Looks Like: Controls that look pushed out of or pressed into one same-colour surface using a light and a dark shadow. It is soft, single-hue and low in contrast.
Use When: smart home panel, music player, calculator, meditation app, device controller, concept demo
Avoid When: Most real products. Edge and state contrast is too weak for many users, so use it only for a few controls and always add a clear label and border.
Palette: One mid-light grey-blue for page and controls, shaded by two shadows, plus one darker accent for text and active state. Base #E4E9F0, light #FFFFFF, shade #B8C2D1, ink #2A3446, accent #3558D6.
Type Approach: Use Poppins or DM Sans at weight 500-600 so labels are stronger than the surface. Body 16px with ink at 7:1 on base.
Layout: Single column with 20px margins, large circular or rounded controls, 24px gaps so shadows do not overlap, thumb-reach bottom row.
Motion: Pressed state swaps raised for inset shadow in 120ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Everything is soft and the same colour so nothing stands out; grey labels on grey surface; shadows on every card; many tints of one colour
Accessibility: The big risk is low contrast: shadows do not count as 3:1 edges (1.4.11), so add a border or accent fill to controls and show state with an icon or text. Text must pass 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Use strong focus rings (2.4.7).
Performance: medium: stacked shadows on many elements slow scrolling; use on a few controls only.
CSS Starter:
.knob { background: #E4E9F0; border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: 6px 6px 12px #B8C2D1, -6px -6px 12px #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #C7D0DD; }
.knob:active { box-shadow: inset 4px 4px 8px #B8C2D1, inset -4px -4px 8px #FFFFFF; }

Aliases: Microsoft Fluent|Fluent UI|Fluent design system
Keywords: fluent, microsoft, windows, office, teams, react, components, tokens
Looks Like: Microsoft's design system for Windows, Office, Teams and its web apps: restrained surfaces, clear hierarchy, subtle depth and well-defined states.
Use When: microsoft 365 add-in, teams app, windows app, enterprise tool, office-like app, internal business app
Avoid When: Brands that need a separate identity or a consumer feel. Hand-copied Fluent looks off, so use the official library and tokens instead.
Palette: Use the official theme tokens and brand ramp rather than picking colours. Starting points: neutral background #FFFFFF, foreground #242424, brand #0F6CBD, danger #B10E1C.
Type Approach: Fluent uses Segoe UI on Windows and system fonts elsewhere. Use the library's type ramp and set no custom display face.
Layout: Follow the official layout guidance: 4px spacing steps, a consistent corner radius, command bars, and panes. Density follows the library's component sizes.
Motion: Use the library's own motion curves and durations; do not write your own timings. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Re-creating Fluent by hand with invented token names; mixing Fluent with Material components; leaving the default blue brand when the product has its own
Accessibility: The official Fluent React components ship with tested focus, keyboard and screen reader behaviour. Keep them intact and check any custom brand colour at 4.5:1 (1.4.3) and focus at 2.4.7.
Performance: medium: use the official package and import components one by one to avoid a large bundle.
CSS Starter:
/* Prefer the official Fluent UI React components; this fallback only shows the idea. */
.btn { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; border-radius: var(--radius); min-height: 32px; }
Checklist: Official Fluent UI package and tokens used; custom brand ramp checked for contrast; dark theme tested; keyboard flow tested; no hand-copied tokens

Aliases: Polaris|Shopify admin design|Polaris web components

Type Approach: Polaris uses the system font stack inside the admin. Use the library's text components and type ramp; do not add a custom face.
Layout: Follow the official page layout: title bar, one or two columns, sections grouped in cards, and list views. Spacing comes from the token scale.
Motion: Use only what the components give; keep custom motion to none. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Writing a lookalike by hand in CSS; using Polaris on a storefront; decorating admin pages with hero images; making every action primary
Accessibility: Official Polaris components handle focus, labels and roles. Do not strip them. Merchants use the admin all day, so keep contrast at 4.5:1 (1.4.3), support keyboard use (2.1.1) and clear error messages (3.3.1).
Performance: low: system fonts and a focused component set; use the official package for current needs.

/* Use Polaris web components or the React library for real work. */

Aliases: Apple HIG|Human Interface Guidelines|iOS native|SwiftUI native
Keywords: apple, ios, hig, swiftui, native, human interface, system, mobile
Looks Like: The look and behaviour of apps built with Apple's own frameworks: system fonts, standard bars, sheets and gestures that users already know.
Use When: ios app, ipad app, mac app, watchos app, app store product, apps that should feel at home on apple devices
Avoid When: Cross-platform brands wanting the same look on Android, or web pages that only imitate it. On the web, do not fake native chrome.
Palette: Use system colours and semantic roles so light, dark and accessibility settings adapt. Fallback starting points: label #000000, background #FFFFFF, system blue #007AFF, grouped background #F2F2F7.
Type Approach: Use the system font (San Francisco) with Dynamic Type text styles. Do not hard-code font sizes in native apps.
Layout: Use the standard navigation bar, tab bar at the bottom, sheets, lists and safe areas. Targets at least 44 by 44 points.
Motion: Use the system's own transitions and springs; they follow platform settings. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Imitating iOS in web CSS with fake status bars; hard-coded colours that break dark mode; custom tab bars that move the back gesture; ignoring Dynamic Type
Accessibility: System components support VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, contrast and reduced motion out of the box; keep them. Test the largest text sizes and increased contrast. Target size 44pt (2.5.8 equivalent) and 4.5:1 text (1.4.3).
Performance: low: native system controls are cheap; avoid custom drawing where a standard control exists.
CSS Starter:
/* On the web this is only a rough fallback; build native screens with SwiftUI. */
body { font: 17px/1.4 -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom); }
Checklist: Standard system components used; Dynamic Type tested at the largest size; dark mode and increased contrast tested; safe areas respected; VoiceOver tested

Aliases: Plain government style|Council website|Gov-style|Plain service design
Keywords: public service, council, school, charity, plain, accessible, government, forms
Looks Like: One column, big plain type, obvious links and buttons, and no decoration. Every page answers one question and starts with what to do.
Use When: council, school, charity, nhs-style service, housing, benefits, forms, local government, community group
Avoid When: Brands that rely on mood or imagery, such as fashion or entertainment. Plain does not mean unfinished: it still needs a clear hierarchy and good words.
Palette: Black text on white, one strong link blue and one action colour, with a bold focus colour. White #FFFFFF, ink #0B0C0C, link #1D70B8, action #00703C, focus #FFDD00.
Type Approach: Use Public Sans or Atkinson Hyperlegible in a single family for headings and body at weights 400 and 700. Body 19px on phones, line height 1.5, measure under 70 characters.
Layout: One column, max width about 40rem, 20px margins, 24px or more between sections, headings that say what the page is for, a prominent start button.
Motion: None needed: no animation. Focus and hover changes are instant. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change. Nothing to swap.
Slop Habits: Welcome banners and hero images with no use; a pill badge above the headline; a bordered box around every block; carousels on key pages
Accessibility: Strong focus (2.4.7, 2.4.11) with a thick high-contrast ring; underline links; 7:1 for text where possible (1.4.3); 44px buttons (2.5.8); label every field and say what went wrong (3.3.1); allow zoom to 200% (1.4.4) and reflow at 320px (1.4.10).
Performance: low: no heavy assets; plain HTML and one font file works well on weak connections.
Checklist: Each page starts with what to do; links are underlined; buttons have clear words; focus ring is thick; forms have labels and clear errors

Aliases: Photocopy zine|Cut and paste|Punk print|Fanzine
Keywords: zine, photocopy, collage, cut and paste, punk, print, band, bookshop
Looks Like: Photocopied-print energy: black ink on coloured paper, cut-and-paste blocks, taped labels and bold type. It is rough on purpose but still easy to read.
Use When: band, bookshop, record label, gig listing, independent maker, market stall, small press, local event
Avoid When: Trust-led services such as law, medicine or finance, and long text pages. Too much roughness hides the dates, prices and buttons people came for.
Palette: Black ink on one or two paper colours, with one fluorescent accent for the single action. Paper #EDE6D3, ink #111111, pink #FF3E8A, yellow #F5E02E, grey #BDB8AB.
Type Approach: Use Special Elite or Courier Prime only for short labels, Bebas Neue or Anton for headlines, and Work Sans for body. Body 16-17px in plain black.
Layout: Overlapping blocks with slight rotation of 1-2 degrees, uneven column widths, taped labels, one image with a rough edge. Keep the key facts in a straight block.
Motion: One 150ms stepped shift on hover; no scroll effects. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, swap movement for an instant state change.
Slop Habits: Tilted stickers on every section; a grid of identical rounded cards; halftone and grain as the only style; monospace for all text
Accessibility: Rough textures behind text break readability, so keep text on flat blocks at 4.5:1 (1.4.3). Rotation must not move links off screen at 320px (1.4.10). Keep tiny cut-out text at 16px or more and 44px targets (2.5.8).
Performance: low: flat colour blocks and CSS borders; compress any scanned image and avoid large textures.
CSS Starter:
.cutout { background: var(--yellow); border: var(--edge); transform: rotate(var(--tilt)); padding: 12px 16px; }
.cutout:hover { transform: rotate(0deg); }
Checklist: Dates and prices sit on flat blocks; tilt is 2 degrees or less; no text on busy texture; one accent action; layout holds at 320px
